objective: Five hours of overall subtraction: remove duplicated implementation and unnecessary internal layers while preserving existing capabilities
changes: Exclude historical evidence tarballs from source distributions, with an archive-content assertion in CI.
Reuse one finite-tensor traversal for native H1 and IsaacLab H1, keeping tensor-only consumers permissive for float metadata.
Use bounded shared stream/file hashing in H1 and Microduck artifact checks; retain Microduck hashing of the loaded file descriptor.
Reuse atomic finite JSON publication for the isolated H1 verifier.
Reuse one validated archive-member iterator in MorphMimic setup and verification; source leaves use the existing regular-file snapshot reader.
Delegate the duplicate Microduck phase blend body to the existing crouch blend, preserving the public function name/signature and numerical gradients.
H1 verifier now derives metadata and optional SHA256 from one opened checkpoint; preflight keeps its original metadata-only result.
MorphMimic verifies the pinned archive checksum and parses members from one opened stream, preventing cache replacement from admitting unpinned source.
Merge contradictory source-distribution paragraphs in docs/README.md into one description matching the archive exclusion and retained report/chart contract.

audit_decisions: Keep public compatibility entry points and SDK-specific result/checkpoint contracts.
Keep SuperMimic source/target CRC and final snapshot rechecks: they protect separate publication and consumption boundaries.
Keep the native and external-SDK training loops separate; their reset/rollout and checkpoint contracts differ.
The archive reduction is measured with the populated cached source manifest, not asserted for every clean checkout.

Keep experimental reports/charts in source distributions: docs/README.md explicitly promises them and test_documentation.py validates the local README/guide links. Only raw historical evidence TARs are excluded.
limits: Source-size reduction reproduces an already populated cached source manifest containing 22 evidence archives; not every clean checkout has that baseline size.
Allocation measurements isolate the hashing expression on a private 128 MiB fixture; they are not whole-training memory or throughput measurements.
Baseline and final CPU fixture workloads differ because the final fixture also tests newly fixed failures; their timing and RSS are not compared as a speed or memory benchmark.
The four-hour final CPU fixture freezes the H1/Microduck/learning/MDP changes with the earlier common MorphMimic reader; the final MorphMimic archive reader has its own 9900-second fixture.
MorphMimic retains 13/18 completed clips with the same detailed episode results as the prior run; five failed clips and tracking quality are not claimed solved by this refactor.
The SuperMimic acceptance is one rollout of the existing seed138 reference checkpoint with all implemented physical gates passing, not a multi-seed or exact IsaacLab V14 reproduction.
